title: Pneumatic — Cross-Bleed Start and Bleed Configuration After a Caution

issue.reason: Issue C. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Crew procedure for a cross-bleed start and for restoring the bleed configuration after a caution, including the timing to expect on a cold aircraft and what to do when the caution clears itself in the climb.

sections.purpose: To give the crew the sequence for a cross-bleed start and the actions to take when a bleed caution appears, including the case where the caution clears itself before top of climb.
sections.description: A cross-bleed start uses air from the running engine to turn the other one, and it depends on the cross-bleed valve opening fully and staying open until the start is complete. On a cold aircraft the valve takes noticeably longer to travel, and on the earlier standard it can take three or four times the normal time on the first start of the day. That delay is not itself a fault, but it does mean that a start begun before the valve is fully open will be slow and may need to be abandoned. The bleed page shows the valve position directly on aircraft at the later standard and infers it from duct pressure on the earlier one, which is why the page can look ambiguous on some aeroplanes and definite on others. A bleed caution in the climb on a warm day, which clears itself before top of climb and does not return, has been a known nuisance on part of the fleet; it must still be actioned and reported, because the whole point of the caution is that you cannot tell a nuisance from a real one in the moment.
sections.crew_procedure: For a cross-bleed start, set the running engine to the thrust called for by the table, select the cross-bleed valve open and wait for the bleed page to show it open before selecting the start. On a cold aircraft allow the longer travel time and do not begin the start early. If a bleed caution appears, action the checklist in full, restore the configuration it leaves you in and continue. If the caution clears itself, do not reset the configuration on your own initiative; leave it as the checklist left it and write the event in the technical log with the level, the temperature and how long the caution stayed on.

type_data.crew_action: Confirm the cross-bleed valve open before selecting start; action and report a bleed caution even if it clears itself.
